set.body:
Defect: Standardizing on n=1 produces a schema shaped like Friends. Memento is the same lab dialect with different everything else: 5 s recall grid vs Friends' 1 s, BroadSceneNum vs WhichEvent, 12 header-layout variants across its own 133 sheets, and presentation order vs story order as separate explicit data.

Do: Write the Memento CorpusProfile. EXPECT THE SCHEMA TO CHANGE and budget for it; record every change the second corpus forces, in the ADR, as the evidence that the schema is real rather than a transcription of Friends.

Tests: Header-variant tolerance is driven by the PROFILE, not by the reader. StoryOrder(Permutation) is declarable.

Mutants (SD1 — each must die, recorded by name): hardcode one header layout -> the variant test must fail. Let the reader sniff column names -> the profile-drives-everything test must fail.

Exit: Two corpora, one profile MECHANISM, no reader change between them. NB the claim 'two dialects are enough to validate the schema' is a judgement, not a measurement; this is where it is tested and it may fail.

Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-17-annotation-intake-contract.md S3, P4
set.title: intake P4: Memento profile -- the schema-breaker
